info.title: IdClawPassport API
info.description: API for AI agent identities backed by RODiT tokens on NEAR, including facial token_id encoding. Canonical OpenAPI document: `GET /openapi.json`.

BearerAuth.description: RODiT-issued JWT access token validated by @rodit/rodit-auth-be (RoditClient.authenticate), obtained via the RODiT login flow (e.g. /api/login). This is not an API key.

TokenId.description: Facial token_id encoding: 12 lowercase letters a-z (11 category indices + 1 checksum).

id.description: Identifier for the verification method fragment.

controller.description: Controller DID for the verification method.

@context.description: Ordered list of JSON-LD contexts used in the DID document.

alsoKnownAs.description: Alternate DID identifiers for the same subject.

controller.description: Controller account for the DID document.

verificationMethod.description: Verification methods available on the DID document.

service.description: Service endpoints advertised in the DID document.

requestId.description: Request correlation identifier returned by the API.

ErrorResponse.description: Unified error response structure. All errors follow this compact format: error object with code and message, plus requestId and timestamp for tracing.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. HOLA HTTP validation uses `HOLA_*` (e.g. HOLA_VALIDATION_FAILED). JWT login verification on POST /api/login uses `LOGIN_CHALLENGE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID` or `LOGIN_BASE64URL_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (and other `RODIT_*` / policy codes) — not `HOLA_*`. Outbound webhook signature failures use `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. Generic codes include RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

details.description: Optional additional context (only included when helpful)

requestId.description: Unique request identifier for tracing (ULID format)

error.message: Token ID must be exactly 12 lowercase letters

200.description: Service health status with dependency checks.

get.summary: Get timestamp and nonce for HOLA handshake

200.description: Returns a timestamp and nonce hex that can be directly concatenated into HOLA handshake messages.

noncetsHex.description: 32 uppercase hex characters (16 bytes) for the nonce component of HOLA handshake. This is the hex-encoded random nonce, already normalized to uppercase. Use this value directly when constructing HOLA messages. Do not attempt to parse or extract from a combined format.

timestamp.description: Server ISO-8601 timestamp when the nonce was generated.

length.description: Number of random bytes used to generate the nonce (always 16).

algorithm.description: Algorithm used to generate the nonce.

500.description: Agent discovery failed due to upstream service errors.

401.description: Unauthorized - JWT token is missing or invalid.

get.summary: Get timestamp for AI agent login
get.description: Public endpoint for AI agents to obtain synchronized timestamp and ISO string needed to construct /api/login requests. Both values are generated from the same moment to ensure signature verification succeeds.

200.description: Authentication parameters for constructing login requests.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds for /api/login payload.

timestamp_iso.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for signing the login message.

429.description: Too Many Requests - rate limit exceeded (default 101 requests per minute per IP; configurable via RATE_LIMIT_PUBLIC_MAX and RATE_LIMIT_PUBLIC_WINDOW_MINUTES).

get.summary: List RODiT token holders with facial descriptions
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of all RODiT token holders with their facial descriptions decoded from token IDs. This is a public endpoint for agent discovery. For detailed identity info including DN and full metadata, use the protected /api/identity/token/{tokenId}/full endpoint.

**Query parameters**: Only **`limit`** and **`cursor`** are supported. Extra parameters (e.g. `owner`) are **ignored** — do not use this endpoint to look up “your” token by NEAR account; save the **`token_id`** returned when the RODiT was minted.

**Current Capabilities**: Browse agents using pagination (`limit` and `cursor`).

**Planned Features**: Search and owner filtering may be added later.

⚠️ **DISCLAIMER**: The creature field and other agent metadata are self-declared by the agent. It is your responsibility to verify the accuracy and authenticity of this information before relying on it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of agents to return (default: 20, max: 100)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor for fetching the next page

200.description: Paginated list of agents with facial descriptions

creature.description: Creature/profession/species from the agent's DN metadata

checksumValid.description: Whether the token ID checksum is valid

categories.description: Facial feature categories with their values

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page, null if no more results

disclaimer.description: Warning that creature field and agent metadata are self-declared and should be verified

get.summary: Get authenticated agent's own DN and facial description
get.description: Returns the caller's own Distinguished Name (DN) and facial description based on their authenticated RODiT token. This endpoint is for self-identification only - it derives the caller's tokenId from the JWT sub field. For looking up other agents, use GET /api/identity/token/{tokenId}/full.

200.description: Authenticated agent's own DN and facial description.

dn.description: Parsed Distinguished Name information from token metadata.

notAfter.description: Token expiration timestamp (ISO8601 format). Null if token has no expiration.

metadata.description: Full token metadata including openapijson_url, not_after, not_before, max_requests, webhook_url, userselected_dn, and userselected_dn_info.

400.description: IdentityUnavailable when sub is missing or unparsable.

error.message: JWT payload is missing required sub field for identity derivation

404.description: IdentityNotFound when NEAR token does not exist.

post.summary: Verify a peer's HOLA using Ed25519 and a Morse-compatible canonical message
post.description:
Peer-verification endpoint for HOLA messages received from another agent. Use `/api/identity/verify` for peer verification; use `/api/testhola` for self-testing your own outbound HOLA generation.

Before full signature/timestamp/token verification, the endpoint performs fail-closed request-shape checks:
- Payload envelope check: `hola` must be a string containing the full HOLA line (not a nested JSON object).
- Transport-shape lint: catches common transport and formatting confusions early.

Early request-shape failures return `400` with:
- `code: HOLA_VALIDATION_FAILED` (same codes as `/api/testhola`; details include `reasonCode`, e.g. `payload_is_json_object`, `unix_millis_timestamp`, `signature_not_base32`, `placeholder_signature`)

For self-correction workflows and richer diagnostics/examples, validate sender-side payloads with `/api/testhola`.

hola.description: Request field containing the HOLA handshake line exchanged between AI agents. CASE-INSENSITIVE: The protocol accepts any case (e.g., 'hola', 'HOLA', 'Hola'). For verification, the server canonicalizes the full signed payload to uppercase before Ed25519 and checksum validation. Token IDs are then normalized to lowercase only for blockchain lookup. STANDARD FORMAT: HOLA/<recipient>/<tokenId>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-ed25519-signature>/<checksum>. SUBAGENT FORMAT (delegated signers): HOLA/<recipient>/<delegateID>/<issuer_tokenId>/<publicKey-base32>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-ed25519-signature>/<checksum>. Base32 variant is RFC 4648 Base32 with alphabet A-Z2-7; uppercase canonical form is used and '=' padding is optional on input. For standard format, the Ed25519 signature is computed over HOLA/<recipient>/<tokenId>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/. For subagent format, the signature is computed over HOLA/<recipient>/<delegateID>/<issuer_tokenId>/<publicKey-base32>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/. The checksum is a single letter from ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ (23 letters; omits I, L, O). Checksum algorithm: sum UTF-16 code units (JavaScript String semantics; ASCII-only prefixes match byte sums) over HOLA/<recipient>/.../<base32-ed25519-signature>/ including trailing slash (everything before this checksum field), modulo 23, index into that alphabet (NOT MD5/SHA). Recipient defaults to MUNDO if not specified. Note: noncets-hex is 32 uppercase hex characters from /api/holanonce16ts (hex-encoded, uppercase). delegateID is the hashOrDelegateId from /api/isauthorizedsigner (DID, name, or BLAKE3 hash). Maximum length: 512 characters. See /api/isauthorizedsigner for subagent authorization validation.

maxAgeMs.description: Maximum allowed age in milliseconds for the hola. Defaults to 300000.

200.description: Verification result with detailed checks.

verified.description: True when all checks pass and the peer hola is accepted.

peerTokenId.description: token_id extracted from the peer hola. For subagent format, this is the issuerTokenId.

destinatary.description: Recipient field extracted from the HOLA message.

isSubagentFormat.description: True when the HOLA message uses the subagent format (11 fields) instead of standard format (8 fields). Only present when true.

delegateId.description: The delegateID from the subagent HOLA message. Only present when isSubagentFormat is true.

issuerTokenId.description: The parent agent's token ID who authorized this subagent. Only present when isSubagentFormat is true.

checks.description: Detailed boolean flags indicating which verification stages passed.

tokenExists.description: True when the peer token exists on NEAR.

tokenActive.description: True when the token is considered active for verification. Currently false when token is expired based on metadata.not_after.

timestampFresh.description: True when the timestamp is within the accepted age window.

nonceReplaySafe.description: True when the nonce has not already been accepted for the same sender token within the active timestamp window.

signatureValid.description: True when the Ed25519 signature matches the canonical message.

checksumValid.description: True when the checksum matches the canonical hola payload.

failureReasons.description: List of machine-readable codes describing why verification failed. Empty when verified is true.

failureDetails.description: Human-readable descriptions for each failureReasons entry.

signatureVerificationImplemented.description: Signals that signature verification is active for this server implementation.

warnings.description: Optional warning entries for suspicious but non-fatal conditions such as recipient mismatch.

400.description: InvalidRequest or InvalidPeerHola - malformed hola string, payload envelope/transport-shape validation failure, or cryptographic/token validation failure.

post.summary: Verify if a public key is authorized to sign on behalf of an IdentyClaw Passport holder
post.description: Validates whether a given Ed25519 public key has been authorized by an IdentyClaw Passport holder to act as a delegated signer. This is the primary mechanism for subagent authorization in OpenClaw. Subagents generate their own Ed25519 keypairs and request authorization from their parent agent. The parent signs the delegation record (tokenId:delegateId:timestamp:publicKey) using its RODiT private key, which is then verified by this endpoint. This enables hierarchical agent organizations where subagents can prove they're authorized by a specific parent without needing their own RODiT tokens.

tokenId.description: The IdentyClaw Passport token ID (12 lowercase letters) of the passport holder (owner) authorizing the signer. The endpoint retrieves this owner's public key from NEAR blockchain to verify the signature.

base64HashOrDelegateSignerId.description: Unique identifier or hash for the delegated signer being authorized. Can be a DID, name, BLAKE3 hash, or any text identifier (1-128 characters). Used to identify which specific delegated signer is being authorized. If using a hash, canonicalization is the agent's responsibility.

unixTimestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) when the authorization was granted. Used to prevent replay attacks and establish temporal context.

publicKey.description: Base64url-encoded Ed25519 public key (32 bytes when decoded) of the delegated signer (the entity being authorized to sign on behalf of the tokenId owner). This is the key we are validating as authorized.

signature.description: Base64url-encoded Ed25519 signature (64 bytes when decoded) created by the tokenId owner's private key, proving they authorized this delegated signer's public key. The signature is computed over the message: tokenId:base64HashOrDelegateSignerId:unixTimestamp:publicKey

200.description: Authorization check completed. Returns detailed verification results regardless of authorization status.

authorized.description: True if the public key is authorized by the passport holder; false otherwise.

tokenId.description: The token ID that was checked.

base64HashOrDelegateSignerId.description: The hash or delegated signer ID that was checked.

checks.description: Detailed boolean flags indicating which verification stages passed.

tokenExists.description: True when the passport token exists on NEAR.

tokenActive.description: True when the token is considered active (not revoked/expired). NOTE: Currently a planned feature - returns true if token exists. Full implementation pending contract metadata support.

publicKeyAuthorized.description: True when the Ed25519 signature is valid and proves the public key is authorized by the passport holder.

failureReasons.description: List of machine-readable codes describing why authorization failed. Empty when authorized is true.

400.description: Invalid request - missing or malformed parameters (tokenId, unixTimestamp, publicKey, or signature).

401.description: Unauthorized - JWT token is missing or invalid.

404.description: NotFound - The specified tokenId does not exist on the blockchain.

post.summary: RODiT client login to obtain a JWT access token
post.description: Delegates to `RoditClient#login_client` (@rodit/rodit-auth-be): Express handler that reads `req.body` after JSON parsing. Signed payload is `identifier + timestamp_iso` (concatenated, no separator) where `identifier` is the chosen `roditid` or `accountid`. Server must have own RODiT config initialized (`getConfigOwnRodit`).

roditid.description: 12-letter on-chain `token_id`; must match the identifier used when signing.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds for the signed payload. If omitted, the server uses `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`. Align with GET /api/login/timestamp when signing.

oneOf.description: Login with `roditid`; signature alias `roditid_base64url_signature` (wire-compatible with login_server).

timestamp.description: Unix seconds for the signed payload; defaults server-side if omitted.

roditid_base64url_signature.description: Same bytes as `base64url_signature`; do not send both signature fields non-empty.

oneOf.description: Login with NEAR implicit `accountid` (64-char hex); signature in `base64url_signature`.

accountid.description: 64-char lowercase hex NEAR implicit account id; signed message is `accountid + timestamp_iso`.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds for the signed payload; defaults server-side if omitted.

oneOf.description: Login with NEAR implicit `accountid`; signature alias `roditid_base64url_signature`.

accountid.description: 64-char lowercase hex NEAR implicit account id.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds for the signed payload; defaults server-side if omitted.

roditid_base64url_signature.description: Same bytes as `base64url_signature`; do not send both signature fields non-empty.

schema.description: Exactly one of `roditid` or `accountid` after trim (not both, not neither). Exactly one of `base64url_signature` or `roditid_base64url_signature`. Deprecated keys `signature`, `account_id` → 400 `LOGIN_PAYLOAD_DEPRECATED`. Ambiguous or missing identifiers / signatures → 400 with codes such as `LOGIN_IDENTIFIER_AMBIGUOUS`, `MISSING_LOGIN_IDENTIFIER`, `MISSING_BASE64URL_SIGNATURE`.

200.description: Login successful. Body includes `jwt_token` and `requestId`; header `New-Token` repeats the JWT.

New-Token.description: Same JWT string as `jwt_token` in the response body.

jwt_token.description: Bearer JWT for subsequent API calls.

requestId.description: Request correlation id from the auth layer.

400.description: Validation error (payload shape, ambiguous identifiers, deprecated keys, etc.).

401.description: Credential verification failed when `SECURITY_OPTIONS.SILENT_LOGIN_FAILURES` is false. Typical `error.code` values include `LOGIN_CHALLENGE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID` (login challenge Unix `timestamp` too far in the future vs server), `LOGIN_BASE64URL_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (base64url Ed25519 over UTF-8 identifier + canonical `timestamp_iso` from GET /api/login/timestamp did not verify), `RODIT_NOT_FOUND`, `RODIT_MISSING_METADATA`, `RODIT_NOT_LIVE`, `RODIT_REVOKED`, `RODIT_FAMILY_MISMATCH`, `SMART_CONTRACT_NOT_TRUSTED`, `SERVER_CONFIG_INCOMPLETE`, `LOGIN_MODE_POLICY_REJECTED_*`, `LOGIN_ERROR`, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. Response uses unified `error` object with optional `error.details.failureReason` mirroring `error.code`.

error.message: Error 102: Login attempt failed: Login challenge timestamp invalid: the Unix `timestamp` from your POST body is too far in the future relative to server time (use the `timestamp` from the same GET /api/login/timestamp response as your login signing payload; check clock skew).

details.failureMessage: Login challenge timestamp invalid: the Unix `timestamp` from your POST body is too far in the future relative to server time (use the `timestamp` from the same GET /api/login/timestamp response as your login signing payload; check clock skew).

error.message: Error 102: Login attempt failed: Login base64url signature invalid: Ed25519 verification failed for the base64url_signature over UTF-8 (roditid or accountid) + canonical timestamp_iso from the login challenge (GET /api/login/timestamp). Wrong key, wrong payload, or wrong encoding (must be base64url, not standard base64).

details.failureMessage: Login base64url signature invalid: Ed25519 verification failed for the base64url_signature over UTF-8 (roditid or accountid) + canonical timestamp_iso from the login challenge (GET /api/login/timestamp). Wrong key, wrong payload, or wrong encoding (must be base64url, not standard base64).

503.description: Authentication service unavailable (e.g. RoditClient not initialized on this instance).

post.summary: RODiT client logout to invalidate the current session

200.description: Logout successful; response body is produced by the RODiT SDK.

post.summary: Request minting of a client RODiT via SignPortal
post.description: Frontend calls this endpoint with tamperproofed values and a locally computed minting fee. The server validates permissions against its own permissioned_routes, recomputes the minting fee, and then delegates to SignPortal to mint a new client RODiT token. Optionally, caller can specify a token_id to use for signing; SignPortal will validate the token.

tobesignedValues.description: Tamperproof payload describing the client RODiT to mint (includes permissioned_routes, max_requests, maxrq_window, not_after, serviceprovider_signature, etc.).

mintingfee.description: Total minting fee computed by the client; must match the server's own calculation or the request will be rejected.

token_id.description: Optional: Caller-provided token ID (12 characters from safe charset). If not provided, SignPortal generates one. Must be valid facial encoding with correct checksum.

tier.description: Optional: Pricing tier for fee calculation. If provided, the server uses tier-specific rate limits and fee structures instead of the formula-based calculation. Tiers: personal (48 requests/60s, variable fee), enterprise (4,999 requests/60s, 1,806 NEAR/year), collectible (496 requests/60s, 1,000 NEAR one-time, immortal).

201.description: Client RODiT minted successfully. Response includes SignPortal result (token_id, signatures, metadata) plus fee_data object containing the exact fee values that were signed (token_id, mintingfee, mintingfeeaccount). Frontend uses fee_data to reconstruct and verify the fee_signature_base64url.

200.description: Client RODiT minted successfully; response body is the SignPortal result including token_id, signatures, and all token metadata.

400.description: Validation error such as missing fields, invalid permissioned_routes, minting fee mismatch, bad date/limits, invalid token_id format, or invalid token_id checksum.

500.description: Server or SignPortal error while attempting to mint the client token.

post.summary: Test HOLA message validation and respond with server HOLA
post.description:
Self-testing endpoint to validate YOUR HOLA message generation before sending to peers. Use `/api/testhola` for self-testing; use `/api/identity/verify` for peer verification.

**Sender Token Matching Requirement:** The authenticated JWT token must be from the same agent that created the HOLA message. For standard agents, the HOLA sender `tokenId` must match your authenticated token. For subagents, authenticate with the SUBAGENT JWT (not parent), even though the HOLA contains the parent `issuer_tokenId`. Mismatches are rejected with `reasonCode: sender_token_mismatch`.

**When to Use:**
- `/api/testhola`: Self-testing to validate YOUR HOLA generation before sending to peers
- `/api/identity/verify`: Peer verification to verify HOLA received from ANOTHER agent

Validation is fail-closed and covers: format sanity, checksum, timestamp freshness, nonce replay, sender token existence, token expiration (`not_after`), blockchain/public-key availability, and Ed25519 signature verification.

Supports both formats:
- Standard: HOLA/<recipient>/<tokenId>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-signature>/<checksum>
- Subagent: HOLA/<recipient>/<delegateID>/<issuer_tokenId>/<publicKey-base32>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-signature>/<checksum>

On rejection, the response includes machine-readable error details under `error.details` with:
- `stage`: validation stage that failed
- `reasonCode`: stable failure classifier for automated clients/tests
- `hint`: remediation hint for common failure modes

Early shape-lint stages (before full parsing) may set `reasonCode` to: `payload_is_json_object`, `unix_millis_timestamp`, `signature_not_base32`, `placeholder_signature`. Each error includes `details.documentation` (relative reference paths) and `details.example` (a corrected snippet for the offending field) so agents can self-correct without external lookup.

**Webhook Emission Behavior:** The server emits `/api/testhola` webhook events to the authenticated peer's configured webhook URL at `/hooks/wake` and `/hooks/agent` only when `WEBHOOK_TEST_ENABLED=true`.

Emitted events:
- `testhola_validation_failed`
- `testhola_response_failed`
- `testhola_validation_success`

hola.description: Request field for the HOLA message to validate. Supports standard and subagent formats. Standard: HOLA/<recipient>/<tokenId>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-signature>/<checksum>. Subagent: HOLA/<recipient>/<delegateID>/<issuer_tokenId>/<publicKey-base32>/<ISO8601-timestamp>/<noncets-hex>/API.IDENTYCLAW.COM/<base32-signature>/<checksum>. Base32 variant is RFC 4648 Base32 (A-Z2-7, uppercase canonical form, optional '=' padding on input). Checksum is one letter from ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ (mod 23 over canonical prefix + signature + '/').

200.description: HOLA message is valid. Server responds with its own valid HOLA.

valid.description: Whether the client's HOLA message is valid.

peerTokenId.description: The token ID from the client's HOLA message.

destinatary.description: Recipient extracted from the client's HOLA message.

peerVerified.description: Whether the client's identity was verified.

hola.description: The server's valid HOLA response signed with roditclient's key pair.

serverTokenId.description: The server's token ID used in the response HOLA.

serverDestinatary.description: Recipient used by the server in its response HOLA.

serverTimestamp.description: The ISO 8601 timestamp used in the server's HOLA response.

warnings.description: Optional warning entries for suspicious but non-fatal conditions such as recipient mismatch.

400.description: HOLA message is invalid, stale, or signature verification failed. Returns detailed reason.
